requests.title: Read back what you wrote: decisions and actions in the v1 portfolio read
requests.answerToSource: Both reads are live, under a `read:meetings` scope that mirrors `write:meetings` rather than riding on `read:portfolio` — INT-02 separated the audit trail so a warehouse feed would not carry governance, and a decision register is the same. Each row carries its `externalId` (which is how `adopt` finds a row you wrote before it had an identity) and its `version`. Actions carry `raisedInStatus`, so a sync can see that an action lives in a closed room before it writes `Open` over the minute of a meeting.
requests.observed: Without them, adopt on a legacy decision or action has no discovery path, no reconciliation of a room is possible without a session, and a sync reopens an action a human closed (measured: H-01 Done on the screen, reopened to Open by an unchanged re-run).

requests.title: The benefit review is a scheduled act: when realise_on passes, an agenda item appears on the owning board's next occurrence, and an unreviewed benefit past its date is a portfolio exception like a tolerance breach
requests.observed: Benefits realise after closure, when the team has dispersed. A date in a table that nothing chases is how value reporting dies.
requests.answerToSource: A benefit whose realisation date has passed unmeasured now raises a portfolio exception like a tolerance breach, notifies the person who owns it, and appears on the next agenda of a board that sees the project — marked OVERDUE, with its target in its own unit. Measuring it clears both. Closed projects count: that is the normal case, which is exactly why the date was never chased.

requests.title: The business case is re-confirmed at every gate and the gate cannot pass without it: extend reconfirmed_gate into a criterion the ladder enforces, comparing expected cost and benefit against the last version
delivered: server/migrations/042 (case_reconfirmation, gate bound follows the ladder)
server/src/routes/portfolio.js (reconfirm records a row per gate)
web/src/views/index.js (verdict, reconfirmer, note, and the history with its delta)
requests.observed: The fields exist; nothing forces them. A stop/continue decision at each gate is the highest-value control a PMO owns and the one most often skipped.
requests.answerToSource: A gate cannot be cleared on a project whose case has not been reconfirmed at THAT gate; the refusal names the gate and the command that answers it. The reconfirmation is a decision, not a checkbox: a verdict (Continue / Continue with conditions / Stop), a named reconfirmer from the directory, a note, and the two figures as they stood — so the next gate reads the delta. `Stop` refuses the next gate. The 1..4 bound of migration 028 now follows the programme's ladder, so a six-gate programme can reconfirm at gates 5 and 6, which it could not before.

requests.title: One ladder per project: a project under a programme with a declared ladder carries exactly that ladder, and an existing book migrates onto it without duplicates
delivered: server/src/wbs.js#scaffoldProject reads the programme's ladder only
requests.measure: Measured on 5.10.0: a programme declared with a six-gate ladder, then a project created under it, carries exactly six gate milestones (Gate A..F, gates 1..6) and no default four.
remaining: A project created under a programme with a ladder has exactly that programme's gates; an existing book migrates without duplicates; the loader's second run still makes no creating writes.
requests.observed: RT365 measured ten milestones where six were intended, and filed it as a defect rather than a preference.
requests.answerToSource: Half of V-8 is already true and was measured again on this round: a project created under a programme that carries a ladder gets exactly that ladder's gates, never both. What you saw is the other half: your sixteen projects were scaffolded BEFORE RBT carried a gate model, and a declared ladder deliberately does not rewrite projects that already exist (D-33.2 — dated gates and filed evidence would move under people's feet). So the gap is the MIGRATION, and it is accepted as such: an explicit act that moves an existing project onto its programme's ladder, adopting the milestones that already match and refusing to duplicate. Until it ships, `adopt` on PUT /api/v1/milestones binds your Gate A..F rows to the scaffolded ones by their predictable ids rather than adding to them.
